title: UniFlow – Real-Time University Class & Learning Platform
subtitle: Role-based class and learning management app for students, teachers, and administrators, built on Quasar and Firebase.
description: Accomplished a centralized university learning platform as measured by 44 routes across 9 domain modules, 77 Vue components, 10 Pinia stores, and 12 Firestore entity schemas, by engineering a role-guarded Quasar (Vue 3) app on Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore.

contribution.label: Solo owner & full-stack engineer
contribution.headline: Designed and built the entire platform alone: architecture, Firestore data model, role-based routing, Pinia state layer, and all 77 Vue components.
scope: Live class sessions with human-readable numeric session codes
Role-based workspaces for Student, Teacher, and Admin
Collaborative study groups with shared resources
Task announcements, submissions, and multi-criteria grading rubrics
Admin panel for faculties, departments, courses, users, and activity logs

problem.statement: University academic workflows are fragmented: schedules, group discussions, task submissions, and lecture notes live in disconnected apps. Teachers lack one tool for live sessions and graded multi-criteria tasks, and administrators lack a central view of faculties, departments, courses, and activity logs.

benefitMatrix.pain: Joining sessions and tracking tasks, groups, and notes across separate tools
benefitMatrix.before: Course info, group chats, and submissions scattered across disconnected apps; random IDs to join a class
benefitMatrix.after: One workspace with a short numeric code to join a live session, plus groups, tasks, and todos in the same app

benefitMatrix.pain: No single tool to run live sessions and grade against several criteria
benefitMatrix.before: Announcements, submissions, and grading handled in separate places
benefitMatrix.after: Task announcements, submissions, and rubric-based grading in one role-specific dashboard

benefitMatrix.pain: No central place to manage the university hierarchy or audit activity
benefitMatrix.before: Faculties, departments, courses, and logs not managed or audited in one place
benefitMatrix.after: A 16-page admin suite with CRUD across the hierarchy, analytics charts, and activity logs

product.problem: Course schedules, group discussions, task submissions, and notes are scattered across disconnected apps. Teachers have no unified tool for live sessions and rubric grading, and administrators have no central dashboard for the academic hierarchy and audit logs.
product.tagline: One workspace for live classes, groups, tasks, and administration.

backend: Firebase service layer (queries and atomic counters)

keyDecisions.challenge: A multi-role app with dozens of pages and dialogs leads to a bloated router file and scattered components.
keyDecisions.decision: Split the codebase into 9 isolated modules under src/modules/, each with its own pages/, components/, and routes.js, aggregated into the central router. Trade-off: manual route aggregation in src/router/index.js.
keyDecisions.outcome: Clear domain boundaries and room to add admin and student features without touching unrelated code.

keyDecisions.challenge: Random Firestore document IDs are hard for students to type when joining an in-person session.
keyDecisions.decision: Added a Firestore transaction in firebaseService.js that atomically increments a metadata/counters document to assign human-readable session numbers. Trade-off: one extra read/write transaction per session creation.
keyDecisions.outcome: Short numeric session codes students can enter to join live classes.

keyDecisions.challenge: Three roles (Student, Teacher, Admin) needed route protection without repeating authorization logic in every view.
keyDecisions.decision: Centralized access control in the Quasar boot/auth.js plugin, checking to.meta.requiresAuth and to.meta.roles against the Pinia user store's current role. Trade-off: every protected route must declare its metadata.
keyDecisions.outcome: Unauthorized users are redirected to /unauthorized or /auth/login before a view mounts.

keyDecisions.challenge: Direct Firestore SDK calls inside components caused tight coupling, duplicated queries, and inconsistent loading and error handling.
keyDecisions.decision: Split each of the 10 Pinia stores into index.js (state/getters) and action.js, keeping Firestore calls in the service layer and store actions. Trade-off: extra action files per store.
keyDecisions.outcome: Network mutations and state caching are centralized, so components stay declarative.

securityReliability: Role-based navigation guard (boot/auth.js) checking requiresAuth and roles route metadata before views mount
Firebase Authentication for sign-in; Firebase security rules authored for Firestore data access
Pinia persisted state for session continuity across reloads
Atomic Firestore transaction for session counter increments
